text: I'll start by listing the workspace and searching for discount-related code.
The bug is clear: a module-level `_used_codes` set is mutated in `apply_discount`, and `is_eligible` rejects any code already in it. Let me confirm with the test run.
The tests confirm the failure pattern: once a code has been applied in the process, later applications return the subtotal unchanged.

args.root_cause: `library/discounts.py` keeps a module-level set `_used_codes` that is never cleared. `apply_discount` adds every applied code to this set, and `is_eligible` returns False for any code already in the set. So the first order using SAVE10 gets the discount, and every subsequent order in the same process silently gets no discount (the subtotal is returned unchanged). This is process-global state, which explains why restarting the service restores the discount for exactly one more order. Discount codes are multi-use promos, so this "one-use" tracking is wrong for them and is not cleared per order. The `is_eligible` check on `_used_codes` is the culprit; the mutation in `apply_discount` is what makes it stick.

args.summary: Root cause: library/discounts.py tracked applied codes in a module-level set `_used_codes` that was never cleared, and `is_eligible` rejected any code already in it. Since SAVE10 is a multi-use promo, only the first order in a process got the discount; later orders silently got none (until restart). I removed the `_used_codes` global, the membership check in `is_eligible`, and the `.add()` call in `apply_discount`, so eligibility depends only on min_subtotal. tests/test_discounts.py now passes (8/8).
